transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time on short notice. As you know, we've received a credible report that our authorized distributor routed some medical-device orders through an unfamiliar sub-distributor in a restricted market. No shipment suspension, regulatory disclosure, contractual notice, or termination decision has been issued yet. Before I approve any written response package, I need to walk through the situation with each of you under our incident-response protocol. Let's go around the room: I'd like to hear first from our sanctions lead on any exposure, then contracts on our distributor agreement provisions, and finally client operations on the hospital systems that depend on our devices for scheduled procedures. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Thank you all three for bringing these critical pieces forward. Let me synthesize what we now have so we can move decisively. Thomas, your screening confirms two shipments to an Iran-linked reseller with no OFAC general license coverage — that gives us clear sanctions exposure requiring immediate shipment suspension and a voluntary OFAC disclosure within 10 days. Maya, the executed distribution agreement requires a written cure notice identifying the offending shipments and giving 10 business days before termination can take effect — so we cannot simply terminate today; we must issue that cure notice now, in parallel with the suspension. Jordan, the hospital network's approved 14-day direct-ship transition arrangement means we can keep critical devices flowing to hospitals for scheduled procedures while distributor shipments are suspended — that covers us beyond both the 10-day OFAC window and the 10-business-day cure period. Here is what I am going to direct as our integrated response: First, we suspend distributor shipments immediately. Second, we issue the written cure notice today, identifying the two offending shipments, starting the 10-business-day clock. Third, we prepare and file the voluntary OFAC disclosure within 10 calendar days. Fourth, we activate the 14-day direct-ship transition arrangement so hospital procedures are not disrupted. Fifth, at the end of the cure period, assuming no cure is effected — which I cannot foresee given the nature of the breach — we terminate the distribution agreement. I will now approve the written response package incorporating all of these elements. Are there any objections before I finalize?
